## Octave Specialty Group Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 09, 2026


- **Insurance Distribution Segment**


- *Total revenue grew* 35% *to $58 million*
- *Organic revenue growth equaled 23%*
- *Net loss to shareholders totaled $(4.2) million, compared to $(5.4) million in 3Q25*
- *Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders totaled $8.3 million, compared to $6.0 million in 3Q25*


- **Specialty P&C Insurance Segment ("Everspan")**


- *Gross and net premiums written totaled $99 million and $26 million, up 2% and 44%, respectively*
- *Net income equaled $1.3 million, compared to a net loss of $(0.1) million in 3Q25*
- *Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders totaled $2.2 million, compared to less than $0.1 million in 3Q25*


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Octave Specialty Group, Inc. (NYSE: OSG) ("Octave" or "OSG"), a global specialty insurance firm, today reported its results for the third quarter of 2026.


Claude LeBlanc, President and Chief Executive Officer of Octave, said "Octave delivered a solid third quarter, with continued growth in our Insurance Distribution business and further progress at Everspan, despite a P&C market that has become more competitive as the year has progressed. While we expect market softening to continue into 2027, we believe that our operating model was built to perform through market cycles, and Octave is well positioned to deliver sustained, profitable growth toward our long-term goals."


LeBlanc continued, "In the third quarter, we grew our Insurance Distribution revenue 35%, including organic revenue growth of 23%. This strong organic growth, well ahead of the broader industry, is consistent with our seasonally adjusted third quarter plan and reflects the strength of our purposely diversified portfolio strategy and the strong embedded value of our scaling MGA incubator. Insurance Distribution Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders was $8.3 million, compared to $6.0 million in the prior-year period.


"Everspan's results continue to reflect the repositioning of its growing programs business. During the third quarter, the combined ratio improved meaningfully from the prior-year period. Specialty P&C Insurance Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders was $2.2 million, compared to less than $0.1 million in the prior-year period. Subsequent to quarter end, Everspan entered into an agreement to sell its redundant admitted shell company, Providence Washington Insurance Company, which is expected to help simplify its operating structure and further strengthen its capital base."

**Third Quarter 2026 Summary(4)**


Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $85.3 million ***,*** an increase of 28% compared to $66.6 million in the prior-year period. The increase was driven by 35% revenue growth in the Insurance Distribution segment, reflecting organic revenue growth of 23% and the acquisition of ArmadaCare, as well as 52% earned premium growth at Everspan.


Octave's net (loss) from continuing operations attributable to shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 improved to $(13.8) million, ** compared to $(31.7) million ** in the prior-year period. The improvement was attributable to (i) the Insurance Distribution segment, which reported a net (loss) to shareholders of $(4.2) million, compared to $(5.4) million in the prior-year period, (ii) the Specialty P&C Insurance segment, where Everspan reported net income of $1.3 million, compared to a net (loss) of $(0.1) million in the prior-year period, and (iii) a reduction in the Corporate net (loss) to $(10.8) million from $(26.3) million in the prior-year period.


Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 improved to $3.3 million, compared to $(2.9) million in the prior-year period. The improvement was driven by a $2.3 million increase in Insurance Distribution Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders. In addition, the third quarter of 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to shareholders improved for Everspan and Corporate by $2.2 million and $1.8 million, respectively, from a year ago.


Adjusted net (loss) to shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 improved to $(1.3) million, compared to $(10.0) million in the prior-year period, reflecting lower interest expense, growth in the Insurance Distribution and Specialty P&C Insurance segments, and a smaller Corporate Adjusted net (loss).

***OSG Corporate (holding company only)***


OSG on a standalone basis, excluding its ownership interests in its Specialty P&C Insurance and Insurance Distribution subsidiaries, had net assets of $45 million as of September 30, 2026. Assets included cash and liquid securities of $24 million and other investments of $21 million.


***Consolidated Octave Specialty Group, Inc. Stockholders' Equity and Noncontrolling Interests ("NCI") Impact to EPS***


Stockholders’ equity attributable to common shareholders at September 30, 2026, was $684 million, or $15.19 per share, compared to $699 million, or $15.52 per share, as of June 30, 2026. The decline was primarily a result of the total comprehensive loss attributable to common shareholders of $(18) million, partially offset by an increase in additional paid-in capital related to share-based compensation of $4 million.

***Non-GAAP Financial Data***


In addition to reporting the Company’s quarterly financial results in accordance with GAAP, the Company is reporting non-GAAP financial measures: EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Organic Revenue Growth Rate (Insurance Distribution segment only), Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Margin. These amounts are derived from our consolidated financial information, but are not presented in our consolidated financial results because they are not calculated in accordance with GAAP.


We present non-GAAP supplemental financial information because we believe such information is of interest to the investment community, and that it provides greater transparency and enhanced visibility into the underlying drivers and performance of our businesses on a basis that may not be otherwise apparent on a GAAP basis. We view these non-GAAP financial measures as important indicators when assessing and evaluating our performance on a segmented and consolidated basis, and they are presented to improve the comparability of our results between periods by eliminating the impact of the items that may not be representative of our core operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are not substitutes for the Company’s GAAP reporting, should not be viewed in isolation, and may differ from similar reporting provided by other companies, which may define non-GAAP measures differently.


The following paragraphs define each non-GAAP financial measure. A tabular reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measure to the most comparable GAAP financial measure is also presented below.


**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


**Organic Revenue (Insurance Distribution Only)** — Organic Revenue is defined as Insurance Distribution segment total revenue for the relevant period excluding (i) the first twelve months of revenue (e.g. commissions and fees) generated from acquisitions, (ii) revenue from divestitures and (iii) other items such as contingent commissions, profit commissions and the impact of changes in foreign exchange rates.


**Organic Revenue Growth** is the change in Organic Revenue period-to-period, with prior period revenue adjusted to (i) include revenue (e.g. commissions and fees) that were excluded from Organic Revenue in the prior period which reached the twelve-month owned mark in the current period, (ii) exclude revenue related to divestitures and (iii) exclude other items such as contingent commissions, profit commissions and the impact of changes in foreign exchange rates.


**Total Specialty P&C Insurance Production** includes gross premiums written by Octave's Specialty P&C Insurance segment and premiums placed by the Insurance Distribution segment. Specialty P&C Insurance revenues are dependent on gross premiums written, as specialty program insurance companies earn premiums based on the portion of gross premiums written retained (i.e., net premiums written) and fees on gross premiums written that are ceded to reinsurers. Insurance Distribution revenues are dependent on premium volume, as Managing General Agents/Underwriters and brokers receive commissions based on the amount of premiums placed (i.e., gross premiums written on behalf of insurance carriers) with insurance carriers.


**EBITDA** — EBITDA is net income (loss) from continuing operations before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization of intangible assets.


**EBITDA Margin —** EBITDA divided by total revenues.


**Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin —** ** We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) from continuing operations before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation, amortization of intangible assets, change in fair value of contingent consideration and certain items of income and expense, including share-based compensation expense, acquisition and integration-related expenses, severance, and other exceptional or non-recurring items, including those related to raising capital. We believe that Adjusted EBITDA is an appropriate measure of operating performance because it eliminates the impact of income and expenses that may obfuscate business performance, and that the presentation of this measure enhances an investor's understanding of our financial performance.


**Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Net Income Margin —** We define Adjusted Net Income as net income (loss) from continuing operations attributable to shareholders adjusted for amortization of intangible assets, change in fair value of contingent consideration and certain items of income and expense, including share-based compensation expense, acquisition and integration-related expenses, severance and non-recurring income and loss items that, in the opinion of management, significantly affect the period-over-period assessment of operating results, and the related tax effect of those adjustments. Per share amounts exclude any impact of revaluing noncontrolling interests as otherwise reported under GAAP earnings per share. We believe that Adjusted Net Income is an appropriate measure of operating performance because it eliminates the impact of income and expenses that may obfuscate business performance.

For more information, visit[www.octavegroup.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.octavegroup.com&esheet=54638105&newsitemid=20261109139723&lan=en-US&anchor=www.octavegroup.com&index=3&md5=79ab340b886482d442a7bdd72ca5babc) .


The Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation of Octave contains substantial restrictions on the ability to transfer Octave’s common stock. Subject to limited exceptions, any attempted transfer of common stock shall be prohibited and void to the extent that, as a result of such transfer (or any series of transfers of which such transfer is a part), any person or group of persons shall become a holder of 5% or more of Octave’s common stock or a holder of 5% or more of Octave’s common stock increases its ownership interest.
